judgement.summary:
Step 4 is NOT acceptable as it stands; two concrete defects must be fixed first, plus three small ones. I re-verified every decisive claim on the code and by probe (throw-away SEMANTIC_DB_DIR only; nothing in the repo was modified; suite reproduced at 353 passed / 3 pre-existing environment failures).

MUST FIX (2):
1. soundness-S1 (major, confirmed by my own probe): the live-path statement refresh sits inside `if seeds:` (semantic_interpretation.py:1426, refresh at :1524-1525), so a live run over a theory with zero seeds takes the `else: # All cached` branch (:1540-1546) and never refreshes. Probe: dry run refreshes `expr` to "c :: nat => nat"; a live run over the same store leaves it at "c :: nat". Step 3 (8683e6f:1350-1353) did the refresh inline in the scan loop, hence on both paths regardless of the todo count, and §5.3.2 (plan:293-297) / §15.8 item 8 (plan:1394-1400) state it unconditionally. Reachable with no preceding dry pass: Tools/semantic_interpretation_app.ML:99-115 (`Semantic_Store.collect`) calls `interpret_with_parallel` directly (isabelle_semantics.py:1308 drives it; `--reinterpret` = force, semantic_store.ML:1922), so under `collect --reinterpret` every already-fresh theory silently keeps a stale `expr` and a vector embedded from it, forever (the next scan sees the digest unchanged). Coverage confirms nothing can catch it: lines 1444 and 1542-1546 are never executed by the suite.
2. agreement-S4-2 (major, confirmed by my own probe): the enrolled-name refusal never fires for a name containing an Isabelle symbol. `enrolled_names` holds `Entry.name` = `pretty_unicode(...)` (:1572, :404) while semantics.py:1766 rewrites the agent's argument with `ascii_of_unicode` before the membership test at :1775. Measured: enrolled "Foo.f₁", the tool reaches `query_by_name_raw` for BOTH the glyph and the escape spelling; the ASCII-only control refuses correctly. The comment step 4 wrote at :1457-1460 and §15.8 (plan:1372-1377) both assert the guarantee that fails. Inherited from step 3, but step 4 makes this list the live guard and step 5's judge turns a miss into a silently wrong "same". No test touches it (`grep -rn "enrolled_names|working_names|Cannot query" archive/tests/` → nothing).

ALSO FIX (3, small): soundness-S2 (the "starting agent with %d entries" log line now prints the theory's entity count, contradicting its own closing partner at :1499-1500); soundness-S4 (derivation 8 is wrong: a self-edge is the NORM — semantic_digest.ML:456-458 puts `deps_of_term (Const (name, T))` in a constant's own dep list and semantic_store.ML:1797 resolves it with the same `key_of` that made the entry's key — so filter it where the graph is built, one clause, provably lossless); gate-S4-3 (three comments describing machinery step 4 deleted: `inv_fields` and "phase 1/3").

REJECTED (2): soundness-S3 (the two spellings of `has_gate_fields` are what §15.5 and §15.8 item 4 prescribe, and the proposed helper would destroy the syntactic `judged ⇒ has_gate_fields` that :1077-1086 relies on) and agreement-S4-3 (the live not-enrolled path is correct — my probe with the cached entry in the MIDDLE returns ['description of c0', 'the stored q', 'description of c2'] with state [_DONE, _NOT_ENROLLED, _DONE] — and §15.10 (plan:1476-1479, :1519-1521) schedules that coverage for the step-5 file on purpose). agreement-S4-4 is rejected too: the `{}` default is unreachable from production (only :1437 with a real cache and :1542 with `entries=[]`), and the proposed all-None default would be a claim that can be FALSE, turning `_write:1077` into a spurious mint.

The other verified properties hold as reported: the scan writes nothing but the refresh, ε is read not written, seeds reproduce step 3's todo set minus the scan-time mint, `_EffStar` is the step-3 closure family moved verbatim, `_write`'s rows match §3, derivations 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 are sound. Once the two must-fix items land with the two regression tests named below, step 4 is acceptable — no further review round is needed.

rulings.title: A live run over a theory with no seeds never refreshes the statement
rulings.rationale: Confirmed on the code and by my own probe, and it is a regression against both the shipped scan and the plan. Code: `if seeds:` at semantic_interpretation.py:1426 encloses the only live-path refresh (:1524-1525); the `else: # All cached` branch (:1540-1546) builds a task with `entries=[]` purely to read `historical_cost()` and falls through to the single return at :1548. Probe (throw-away SEMANTIC_DB_DIR, one cached and fresh record whose stored expr is 'c :: nat' while the wire prop_str is 'c :: nat => nat'): `dry seeds = 0`, expr after the dry run 'c :: nat => nat'; after resetting and running LIVE, expr stays 'c :: nat'. Step 3 refreshed inline in the scan loop (8683e6f:1350-1353, inside `if cached and not stale:`), i.e. on both paths regardless of the todo count. The plan states it with no seed-count condition: §5.3.2 (plan:293-297) 'On the live path it runs after the loop', §15.8 item 8 (plan:1394-1400). Consequence: the record keeps an expr that no longer matches the printed statement and — since `update_expr` (semantics.py:760) is what tombstones the vector — its vector stays embedded from the stale statement; the next scan finds the digest unchanged, so the divergence is permanent. I refute the finding's stated route (run_semantic_interpretation DOES dry-run first, Tools/interpret_command.ML:99 before :150) but a worse one holds: Tools/semantic_interpretation_app.ML:99-115 (`Semantic_Store.collect`) calls `interpret_with_parallel` with no dry pass at all, driven by isabelle_semantics.py:1308-1311, and with `--reinterpret` (force, semantic_store.ML:1922) every theory of the cone goes live, virtually all with zero seeds. Coverage proves the suite cannot see it: on the whole suite, lines 1444 and 1542-1546 of semantic_interpretation.py are never executed.
rulings.fix: Make the refresh unconditional on the live path. Preferred shape (one call site, so no future branch can forget it): delete the call at :1524-1525 and put a single `_refresh_statements(entries, rec_cache, not_enrolled)` immediately before the `return InterpretationResult(...)` at :1548, with a one-line comment saying why the scan's `not_enrolled` is the right list. It is safe there today and in step 5: `rec_cache` is the same object the task holds (:563 / :1441), every entry that leaves _NOT_ENROLLED is written by `_write` with `expr=e.prop_str` and its written record is put back into `rec_cache` (:1089, :1095), so the guard `rec.expr != e.prop_str` is a no-op for them and the extra indices cost nothing. The dry path keeps its own call at :1399 (it returns early). TRAP to avoid: do NOT patch the `else` branch with a `task.state`-derived list — in that branch `task` has `entries=[]` and `state=[]`, so the list is silently empty and the bug survives. Two call sites (adding one to the else branch) also works but is the shape that drifted in the first place. REQUIRED regression test: a live `interpret_file` over a store whose single entry is cached and fresh but whose wire `prop_str` differs — assert the driver is never constructed, `res.interpretations` is the stored text, and the record's `expr` was refreshed while its five gate fields stayed byte-identical. That test fails on today's code and also gives lines 1542-1546 their first coverage.

rulings.title: The enrolled-name refusal in `query` never fires for a name containing an Isabelle symbol
rulings.rationale: Confirmed on the code and by my own probe. `Entry.name` is the Unicode glyph form (`name=pretty_unicode(name)`, semantic_interpretation.py:1572) and `enqueue` appends exactly that (:404); `interpret_file` hands the same mutable list to the tool (:1461-1462). semantics.py:1766 overwrites the argument with `ascii_of_unicode(name)` BEFORE the membership test at :1775, so the two spellings can never be equal for a symbol-bearing name. Converter check with the repo's own functions: pretty_unicode('Foo.f\\<^sub>1') -> 'Foo.f₁', ascii_of_unicode('Foo.f₁') -> 'Foo.f\\<^sub>1'. Probe driving `mk_query_by_name_tool` with `query_by_name_raw` replaced by a raiser (no Isabelle, no cache): enrolled 'Foo.f₁' typed as the glyph -> reached query_by_name_raw; typed as the escape form -> reached query_by_name_raw; ASCII-only control 'Foo.plain' -> 'Cannot query "Foo.plain" — it is or will be your task to interpret it from the source.' So for such an entity there is NO input that triggers the refusal, and `Semantic_DB.query` (semantics.py:789-812) has no in-flight suppression of its own. This is exactly the failure §15.8 says the refusal exists to prevent (plan:1372-1377) and that step 4's own new comment asserts is prevented (:1457-1460). The defect is inherited (step 3 passed `working_names = [e.name for e in task.entries]`, equally Unicode) — but step 4 is the step that promotes this list to the live gate-correctness guard and writes the guarantee into a comment, and step 5's judge is what turns a miss into a silently wrong 'same' verdict on a real change. No test covers the refusal at all: `grep -rn 'enrolled_names|working_names|Cannot query' archive/tests/` returns nothing. Severity major, not blocker, because harm still needs the agent to disobey the tool description, and step 4 runs only against a throw-away store (§15.11).
rulings.fix: Compare the two names in ONE spelling. Either normalise the input to the list's spelling — at semantics.py:1775, `if working_names and pretty_unicode(name) in working_names:` (one conversion per call; correct for both spellings the agent can type, since `ascii_of_unicode` is idempotent on the escape form) — or normalise the list, `name in map(ascii_of_unicode, working_names)`. Keep the list shared by reference (do the conversion per call, not at tool-build time) so the refusal still follows enrolment. Add a two-line comment at the site saying that `working_names` carries the glyph spelling the agent was shown while `name` has already been rewritten to the escape form. Do NOT instead store the escape form in `enrolled_names` (:404): that attribute is the names as shown to the agent, and it would push spelling knowledge into the task for one consumer's benefit. Cosmetic rider: the refusal message at :1777-1779 echoes the escape form back at an agent that typed the glyph — bind the raw argument before :1766 and use it in the message text only. REQUIRED test (self-contained, does not wait for step 5): a unit test of `mk_query_by_name_tool` with a stub connection exposing `.server.logger` and `semantics.query_by_name_raw` monkeypatched to a raiser — a symbol-bearing enrolled name is refused when typed in either spelling, and an unrelated name still reaches `query_by_name_raw`. Both refusal cases fail on today's code.

rulings.title: The "starting agent" host-log line counts every entry of the theory, not the entries the agent is asked about
rulings.rationale: Confirmed by reading both versions. The task is now constructed over ALL entries (:1437-1442) and only seeds are enrolled (:1445-1446, the sole `enqueue` call site in the file), but the log line at :1481-1483 still reads `len(task.entries)`. In step 3 the constructor took `entries=[entries[i] for i in uncached]` and the identical line (8683e6f:1438-1440) therefore printed the number of entries the agent would be asked about. So the same sentence now prints a different quantity: on a theory of 500 entities with 3 seeds it says 'starting ClaudeCode agent ... with 500 entries' and the very next line inside the loop says 'agent: sending 3 entries'. It also contradicts its own closing partner at :1499-1500, which already reports `task.enrolled()` ('agent finished, %d/%d interpreted'). This is a host-log line: it appears nowhere in §12 (plan:763-822 lists only writeln/error/report texts) or §15.8, so it is not step 8's business, and the implementer did edit the sibling host-log line in this step (the dry-run 'at least' at :1400-1401, derivation 5). Not a style remark — a concrete behaviour change this step introduced.
rulings.fix: At semantic_interpretation.py:1483 replace `len(task.entries)` with `task.enrolled()`. Prefer it over `len(seeds)`: it is numerically the same at that point, it makes the opening line and the closing line at :1499-1500 report the same quantity, it is the `state`-derived count §15.8 fixes for these numbers, and it stays honest in step 5 when a CHANGED verdict enrols dependents and N legitimately grows. No other change: `task.entries` is used elsewhere only for index lookups (:1069, :1111, :1167, :1521).

rulings.title: Derivation 8: a self-edge in the reverse graph is the norm, not a corner case
rulings.rationale: Derivation 8's framing is wrong and I verified the chain on the ML side. `sem_constant` returns `unions (cls_dep :: abbrev_deps :: deps_of_term (Const (name, T)) :: map deps_of_term props)` (Tools/semantic_digest.ML:456-458); `deps_of_term` maps `Const (name, T)` to `(ConstantK, name)` (:243-252, and `is_synthetic_const` at :202 only strips the `Semantic_Digest.` prefix); `attach` resolves every dep with `Universal_Key.key_of NONE context` (Tools/semantic_store.ML:1797), the same function and context that produced the entry's own key (:1468, :1540). So for every WIP constant — and for classes — `e.deps` contains `e.universal_key`, and the loop at semantic_interpretation.py:1381-1385 appends `i` to `dependents[i]`. That is the common case, not an accepted edge case. Nothing in step 4 reads `dependents`, so no behaviour is wrong today and the code is literally what §15.8 item 5 prescribes — hence minor, and a judgement on the derivation rather than a step-4 bug. In step 5 the self edge would take `_propagate`'s `_DONE` arm for EVERY CHANGED verdict (plan:1128-1131 calls `_propagate` after `_write`, which sets `state[idx] = _DONE` as its last statement, :1096), costing one full `gate_write` transaction that rewrites the record with identical gate fields. I checked that it is provably a no-op rather than a needed raise: the freshly written record has `version == v` and `interpreted_at = ia = max(v, old-self-contrib, others)`, the old self contribution is bounded by `max(v_old, others) <= max(v, others)` since the mint exceeds the stored version, so the recomputation gives exactly `max(v, others) = ia` — it can neither raise nor lower. It also makes the `_DONE` branch mean what its comment says ('an entity already written this run', i.e. someone else).
rulings.fix: Filter the self edge where the graph is built, semantic_interpretation.py:1381-1385: `if j is not None and j != i: dependents[j].append(i)`, with a two-line comment saying that a constant's dep list contains its own key (semantic_digest.ML's `deps_of_term (Const (name, T))`), that the entity's own version is already eff*'s floor so the edge can carry no signal, and that following it would make every CHANGED verdict re-write its own record unchanged. The reverse graph is the only place the self edge has any effect, so it is the only place to filter it. Do NOT strip the self dep from `e.deps` (neither in `_write:1082` nor on the ML side): the stored dep list is the moment-in-time imprint §4.3 compares by value at :1354, so dropping it on one side marks every constant stale forever and on both sides costs a one-off re-interpretation of every stored constant.

rulings.rationale: Confirmed at both named sites, and a third belongs with them. (a) archive/tests/test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py:326-331 is one comment block whose first line step 4 DID rewrite (working_tree.diff hunk at line 795: '# --- the step-3 gate over the store' -> '# --- the gate over the store'), while :328-329 still say the task is built 'over two entries with the scan's (version, interpreted_at) pair set by hand'. That pair is gone: `_gate_task` at :348-355 now passes `rec_cache={...: None, ...: None}` and `InterpretationTask.__init__` (semantic_interpretation.py:549-554) has no `inv_fields`; `grep -rn 'inv_fields|version_to_write|ia_snapshot'` over the package and tests returns nothing. The `_gate_task` docstring three lines below was updated in the same hunk, so the block now contradicts the function it introduces. (b) archive/tests/test_eff_star.py:123,125 say 'Production's phase-3 verdict' and '(phase 1)'; step 3 had those markers (8683e6f lines 1148/1188/1316) and step 4 deleted them — `grep -n phase Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantic_interpretation.py` now returns nothing — and the plan retires the vocabulary (§5.2's heading, plan:171, is 'Scan (replaces phases 1–3)'). (c) The challenger's extension is right: archive/tests/test_incremental_criteria.py:174, in the file step 4 rewrote most, reads '# rebuild the store per order: phase 1 must see identical initial state' — both halves false, since the sibling test three functions up now asserts the dry run writes nothing. Step 8 will not sweep these: §11's grep set (plan:745-753 — metering, quote, actual work, by construction, would be asked) hits only test_incremental_criteria.py:102 and :148. These are not 'consider adding a comment' remarks: each line asserts something about the code that is false, which the project's terminology and load-bearing-comment rules forbid. rulings.fix: Three one-line edits, deleting the dead reference rather than re-explaining the criterion. (1) test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py:328-329: 'an `InterpretationTask` over two / entries whose `rec_cache` says the store holds neither', matching the `_gate_task` docstring step 4 already updated. (2) test_eff_star.py:123 and :125: drop the two phase parentheticals only — 'The scan's staleness verdict per key ...' and '... own version read as ε when it is None or 0, exceeds its ...'. Keep the wording 'None or 0': production is `rec.version or epsilon` (:1367), so ε is read for both, and rewording it as 'a version-less record' would lose the 0 case. (3) test_incremental_criteria.py:174: '# rebuild the store per order: both orders must start from identical state'.

rulings.title: `has_gate_fields` is spelled out twice; the scan and `_write` must agree and nothing makes them
rulings.rationale: The plan prescribes exactly this shape, so there is no plan/code disagreement, and the proposed fix is a downgrade. §15.5 (plan:1163-1168) says 'Two predicates, each defined once and keyed on the digest, never on the kind' and in the SAME sentence cross-references the scan's copy approvingly, '(the scan's own test, :1101)'; §15.8 item 4 (plan:1333-1334) instructs the scan to compute `has_gate_fields = digest or deps` under §15.5's name. 'Each defined once' contrasts one definition line per predicate against re-inlining the condition in each branch — it is not a claim that the module has one copy. The proposed module-level helper is worse where it matters: `has_gate_fields = judged or bool(e.deps)` (:1071) makes `judged ⇒ has_gate_fields` syntactically evident, and that implication is load-bearing — in the judged branch :1078-1079 sets version/baseline/digest unconditionally while :1082 and :1085-1086 guard `deps` and `ia` on `has_gate_fields`, so a judged entry with `has_gate_fields` false would be written with a version and a digest but `interpreted_at=None`, which the next scan reads as 0 (:1367-1368) and calls permanently stale. Routing :1071 through a helper buries that and re-spells the digest test anyway. The drift the finding fears has no concrete failure attached; it is a hypothetical. One measured fact underneath the finding is nevertheless true and worth recording: I mutated the scan at :1344 in a scratch copy of the tree (repo untouched) and the whole suite's failure set stayed byte-identical — deleting the `bool(e.deps)` disjunct is invisible to all 353 tests, even though it disables the eff* test for every cached theorem-alike entry, i.e. a theorem is never re-interpreted after its definition mints. That gap is pre-existing (step-3's `tracked` at 8683e6f:1325 is the same predicate) and is not what the finding claims.
rulings.fix: No code change. Optional, not required for acceptance and NOT the finding's fix: add a six-line scan test for the untested disjunct in archive/tests/test_incremental_criteria.py, whose `_entry` at :68 already takes the digest as a parameter — a cached theorem-alike entry (`_entry('thm', None, [_uk('up')])`, its own record `_put('thm','t',None,[_uk('up')],1,1)`) with the upstream fresh (assert `_dry == 0`) and then minted above it (assert `_dry == 1`). I wrote and ran exactly that: it passes on today's code and fails on the mutant.

rulings.title: No live-path test ever has a not-enrolled entry, so three step-4 deliverables are unpinned
rulings.rationale: The measurement is right, the conclusion is not. Coverage over the whole suite (353 passed) reports semantic_interpretation.py missing lines 1414, 1417, 1444, 1520, 1542-1546: the prefill body `task.results[i] = results[i]` (:1444), both cached-entry report branches and the entire no-seeds branch never execute, so no live `interpret_file` test has a single cached entry. But the code on that path is CORRECT, which I verified rather than argued: a probe over a throw-away store with the cached, fresh entry in the MIDDLE of the wire order ([a, q, z], q stored with a matching digest, version 1, interpreted_at 1, stored expr 'q :: nat' against a wire 'q :: bool') gives state [_DONE, _NOT_ENROLLED, _DONE], `enrolled_names == ['Foo.a','Foo.z']`, a prompt that names neither Foo.q nor anything else unasked, `res.interpretations == ['description of c0', 'the stored q', 'description of c2']` (so the prefill and the `results = list(task.results)` remap are index-exact), q's expr refreshed to 'q :: bool' and its five gate fields byte-identical. And the plan defers this coverage deliberately: §15.10 (plan:1476-1479) moves the dep-edge test's live half 'to the enrolment test of the new file with a cross-reference so the coverage is visibly moved, not dropped' — the cross-reference is in the code at test_incremental_criteria.py:133-136 — and plan:1519-1521 has the step-5 file drive `interpret_file` with a fake driver over an isolated store, over §10's scenario (plan:662-666) in which only A is a seed and B, C are fresh dependents, i.e. two not-enrolled entries by construction. §15.10's rule is that each test edit lands in the commit that breaks the old assertion; step 4 breaks no assertion here. The one part of this hole that did hide a real defect is the zero-seed branch, and that is soundness-S1, whose fix I require to come with its own regression test. Also note the finding's own fix as written would not pin what it claims: with the cached entry LAST, task order coincides with wire order on every asserted position, so a mis-mapping would still pass.
rulings.fix: No change required for step 4. The step-5 file (§15.10) must carry the enrolment test with at least one not-enrolled entry NOT in last position, so that the wire-order/task-order identity at :1539 is genuinely pinned; and if the `scripted_run` fixture is extended there, give it the entry list as a parameter rather than editing the shared `[_TRACKED, _UNTRACKED]`, whose two existing tests (:478, :491) assume every entry is a seed.

rulings.title: `rec_cache` defaults to `{}`, which builds a task whose every gate raises a bare KeyError
rulings.rationale: The mechanics are right but there is no reachable failure, and both halves of the proposed fix are wrong — so this does not carry against derivation 3, which stands. Reachability: `InterpretationTask` is constructed in exactly two production places, :1437 (live, passing the scan's `rec_cache`, which :1334-1337 builds total over `entries` by construction) and :1542 (`entries=[]`, where a gate cannot run since `_gate` indexes into `entries`); the one test that takes the default (test_interpretation_driver.py:51) has the gate body monkeypatched away (:96-100). Proposed fix (a), a required keyword, does not make the lookup total — it only forces two callers with no entries and no gates to type `{}`. Proposed fix (b), defaulting to `{e.universal_key: None for e in entries}`, is actively unsound: it is not 'the honest the store holds nothing for these' but an unconditional claim that can be false, and when false `_write:1077` (`rec.version if rec is not None and rec.version else w.counter_value()`) silently replaces a committed version with a fresh counter read — the exact rollback the :559-562 comment exists to prevent. The cited 'symptom' is not boilerplate either: test_semantic_change_gate_storage.py:350-355's dict is the test's statement of store contents (its docstring says so), and :394-402 proves it, since that store DOES hold records for the dep and upstream keys while `rec_cache` covers only the entry, and `_EffStar._rec_of` (:911-914) reads them lazily. What survives is a small inelegance (the module declares one record source, 'rec_cache ∪ store', and `_gate` uses a stricter second one) and a poor failure message — not worth a signature change.
rulings.fix: No change required. If the implementer nevertheless wants the lookup total by construction, the only shape that is total AND truthful is to reuse the source the module already declares: hoist `_EffStar._rec_of`'s two-line body into one module-level helper (`if k not in rec_cache: rec_cache[k] = Semantic_DB[k]; return rec_cache[k]`), call it from both `_EffStar._rec_of` and `_gate:1113` — `Semantic_DB[k]` returns None for an absent key (semantics.py:621-625), a miss then reads the CURRENT store rather than a pre-run record so §3's no-rollback rule is untouched, and the line finally matches its own comment, 'the record as currently stored'. The alternative, if a miss should stay a hard error, is one assert at :1113 naming the entity. Either is optional polish; do not change the default or the signature.

findings.title: A live run over a theory with no seeds never refreshes the statement — a regression against the shipped scan and against §5.3.2
findings.claim: The live-path statement refresh sits INSIDE `if seeds:`. When a theory's entries are all cached and fresh, `interpret_file` takes the `else: # All cached` branch (:1539), which builds a task only for `historical_cost()` and returns — `_refresh_statements` is never called. Today's shipped scan (8683e6f) refreshed the `expr` inline in the scan loop and therefore did it on the live path regardless of the todo count. §5.3.2 says the refresh runs "after the loop" on the live path with no seed-count condition, and the whole reason it exists is the case where a theory quotes zero: an `expr`-only change must still be refreshed and its vector tombstoned.
findings.evidence:
Probe over a throw-away SEMANTIC_DB_DIR (one cached, fresh entry whose wire `prop_str` is "nat => nat" while the stored `expr` is "nat"):
  working tree  -> `dry seeds = 0`, `expr after dry = nat => nat`; then, after resetting the record, `expr after LIVE run = nat`  (NOT refreshed)
  `git show 8683e6f:...` (step 3), same store, same entry -> `OLD expr after LIVE run = nat => nat`  (refreshed)
Reachable in production without a preceding dry run: `run_semantic_interpretation` "deliberately does NOT go through" `update_interpretations` (semantics.py:1841-1844); it reaches Tools/semantic_store.ML:2341 -> `interpret_with_parallel` -> `interpret_cone` -> `interpret'` (:1860), which calls the live `interpret_file` for every theory of the cone with no dry pass. Every zero-seed theory in that cone silently keeps a stale `expr` and a vector embedded from it. (The refresh does work when the theory has at least one seed: a second probe over a mixed theory — one non-seed with a changed `prop_str`, one uncached seed — ends with `expr of a after : new stmt`, refusal list `['Foo.b']`, results `['stored text', 'fresh text 1']`.)
findings.fix: Run the refresh on the live path unconditionally. Minimal: add `_refresh_statements(entries, rec_cache, not_enrolled)` to the `else: # All cached` branch (with no seeds nothing was enrolled, so `not_enrolled` from the scan IS the final not-enrolled set). Cleaner, and the shape that cannot drift: hoist the single call out of the `if seeds: / else:` pair to just before `return InterpretationResult(...)`, over `[i for i, st in enumerate(task.state) if st == _NOT_ENROLLED]` when a task ran and `not_enrolled` otherwise — it is still on the success path only, since every failure raises earlier.

findings.title: The "starting agent" host-log line now counts every entry of the theory, not the entries the agent is asked about
findings.claim: `_log.info("interpret_file: starting %s agent on %s with %d entries", driver_name, model or ..., len(task.entries))`. Step 4 made the task span ALL of the theory's entries, so `len(task.entries)` is now the theory's entity count, while the agent is only ever sent the seeds. findings.title: Derivation 8: a self-edge in the reverse graph is the NORM, not a corner case — every constant depends on itself
findings.claim: Derivation 8 treats `dependents[j]` possibly containing `j` as an accepted edge case. WHAT I CONFIRMED

1. Code shape. `semantic_interpretation.py:1426` opens `if seeds:`; the live statement refresh is at :1524-1525, inside that branch. The `else: # All cached` branch (:1540-1546) builds an `InterpretationTask(..., entries=[], ...)` purely to read `task.historical_cost()` and falls straight through to `return InterpretationResult(...)`. `_refresh_statements` (:1023-1036) is therefore never called on a live run whose theory has zero seeds. `grep update_expr` over the package shows :1036 is the ONLY expr-refresh route in the interpretation pipeline (the other hits are `migrate_del_padding.py` and the `semantics.py` definition at :760), so nothing else picks it up.

2. Probe (throw-away SEMANTIC_DB_DIR, one cached+fresh record whose stored `expr` is "nat" while the wire `prop_str` is "nat ⇒ nat"):

3. Consequence. A record keeps an `expr` that no longer matches the printed statement, and — because `update_expr` is what tombstones the vector (semantics.py:760) — its vector stays embedded from the stale statement forever. Nothing later re-checks: the next scan finds the record fresh (digest unchanged), so it is a permanent silent divergence, exactly the case §5.3.2 was written for.

WHAT I REFUTED — the finding's reachability argument

The finding says the live path is reached "with no dry pass" via `run_semantic_interpretation` → semantic_store.ML:2341. Both halves are wrong:

THE ROUTE THAT DOES HOLD (replace the evidence with this)

`Semantic_Store.collect` — `Tools/semantic_interpretation_app.ML:99-115` — calls `Semantic_Store.interpret_with_parallel cfg_context force (map Context.Theory thys)` directly, with no dry pass anywhere. It is driven by the `semantics_manage collect` CLI (`isabelle_semantics.py:1308-1311`: `await c.run_app("Semantic_Store.collect")` then `await c._write(targets, args.reinterpret)`), and `--reinterpret` is that `force` bool (`isabelle_semantics.py:1506-1507`). That is the DB-building/refresh path used after an Isabelle/AFP bump — precisely when printed statements change without digests changing — and under step 4 every one of those theories silently keeps a stale `expr` and an un-tombstoned vector. The non-force resume case (a previous collect that wrote every entry but died before `mark_interpreted`, semantic_store.ML:2012) reaches the same branch.

Severity "major" survives the correction. And the design point is independent of any route: the code must not depend on some caller happening to have dry-run first — §5.2/§5.3.2 make the live refresh unconditional, and the current shape leaves "every entry this run did not write has a fresh statement" true in one branch of an `if` only.

I tried to refute this on three fronts and failed on all three; only two sub-arguments inside the finding need correcting.

(1) Is the self-edge really the norm? YES, for constants and classes, and the finding's chain is exactly right. `sem_constant` (Tools/semantic_digest.ML:456-458) returns `unions (cls_dep :: abbrev_deps :: deps_of_term (Const (name, T)) :: map deps_of_term props)`, and `deps_of_term` (:243-252) turns `Const (name, T)` into `(ConstantK, name)` — `filter_out is_synthetic_const` (:249, with `is_synthetic_const` = "has the synthetic prefix", :202) never strips a real constant name. `attach` (Tools/semantic_store.ML:1798-1804) maps every dep through `dep_uk` = `Universal_Key.key_of NONE context (Constant n)` (:1797), which is the very same function and arguments that produced the entry's own `uk` (:1468/:1540). So the entry's own key is in its own dep list. Two refinements to the finding's wording: (a) deps exist only for WIP theories (`val wip = not (Theory_Hash.is_persistent ...)`, semantic_store.ML:1778; a persistent theory gets `[]` at :1780-1782) — irrelevant as an objection, since the gate only ever runs on WIP entries; (b) it is not literally "every entity": theorem-alike entries never self-edge (a theorem's key is not a ConstantK key), types self-edge only when recursive, classes do self-edge via the sorts of their own axioms (`map deps_of_term (Thm.prop_of def :: props)` in `sem_class`, plus `param_deps`). "Every WIP constant, and classes too" is still overwhelmingly the common case, not a corner case — derivation 8's framing is wrong.

(2) Does the self-edge actually reach `_propagate`'s `_DONE` branch in step 5? YES. The plan's gate loop calls `_propagate(task, idx)` only after `minted = _write(...)` (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:1128-1131), and `_write` ends with `task.state[idx] = _DONE` (semantic_interpretation.py:1096). So for a CHANGED verdict the self edge always lands on the `_DONE` case (plan :1208-1216) — the "snapshot raise", i.e. one full `gate_write` transaction.

(3) Is that extra write really a no-op (so: pure waste, no hidden benefit that would argue for keeping the self edge)? YES — verified, not argued. Probe 1 (a `_gate` run over a throw-away SEMANTIC_DB_DIR with `deps=[own_uk, dep_uk]`, then the minted write and the `_DONE` branch replayed by hand) printed `recomputed ia ... == written: True` and `record identical after the self-edge snapshot raise: True`; `update_gate_fields` invalidates no vector (semantics.py:975-986), so nothing else happens either. Probe 2 (3000 random 5-node graphs, every node self-edged, random None/0/1/3/5/9 versions and interpreted_at, including cycles and inverted counters) found 0 trials where the recomputed `interpreted_at` differed from the one `_write` committed. I also confirmed the self edge carries no information on the other two call sites: in the scan's staleness test (`eff.eff_value(rec.version or epsilon, e.deps)`, :1367) and in `_write`'s snapshot (:1085) the self contribution is either walled to `ver` (≤ the entity's own version) or equals `eff*` over the same dep set, so the max never moves.

The finding's ONE bad sub-argument: "same rec_cache, same deps, same version". `rec_cache` is NOT the same — `_write` computes `ia` at :1085 while `task.rec_cache[uk]` still holds the OLD record, and only assigns the new one at :1095, so `_propagate`'s fresh `_EffStar` walks a rec_cache in which the entity's record HAS changed. The identity holds for a different reason: the freshly written self record has `version == interpreted_at == the mint`, so `_contrib` (:918-928) walls it to `ver`, and every other contribution is bounded by the mint. The conclusion survives; the stated reason does not. Its second sub-argument is also loose: "Tarjan ignores the self loop because `index[d] < low[k]` is `0 < 0`" is only the root case; the general reason is that `low[k] <= index[k]` holds at every node, so `index[k] < low[k]` is false wherever the self edge is scanned (:964-966).

So the finding stands: derivation 8 accepts as an edge case something that fires on essentially every constant, and the cost in step 5 is one redundant identical LMDB write transaction per CHANGED constant. It is not a step-4 defect (nothing reads `dependents` in step 4 — grep shows the only readers are the constructor at :554-566 and the hand-off at :1441 — and the code is literally what §15.8 item 5 prescribes), so "minor" is the right severity: it is a judgement against derivation 8 plus a one-clause pre-emption of step-5 waste, exactly what the scope asked for.

With a symbol-bearing enrolled name the refusal misses for BOTH spellings the agent could possibly type — the Unicode form it was shown (normalised away to ASCII) and the ASCII form (already ASCII, still not equal to the Unicode list entry). So for such an entity there is no input at all that triggers the refusal; the tool always falls through to `query_by_name_raw` -> `Semantic_DB.query(uk, ...)` (semantics.py:1660-1661), which returns the stored interpretation whenever a record exists — i.e. precisely the re-interpretation case the guard exists for.
